title: Measurement Validity in LLM Cultural Alignment
abstract: arXiv:2608.29266v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Researchers increasingly treat LLM survey responses as a proxy for human cultural values. This includes projecting model outputs onto instruments like the Inglehart-Welzel Cultural Map and drawing conclusions about which cultures a model resembles. While a model's answer to a value-laden questions may be interpreted as a cultural signal, it also carries sampling noise and, can be quite sensitive to question framing. In this paper, we separate survey responses, sampling noise and question framing for multiple LLMs. We decompose response variance from these models into variation across random seeds, prompt rewordings. We employ noise-to-signal ratio (NSR) to test whether a model's apparent cultural position is distinguishable from noise. When applied across a dozen models from four geographic origins, calibrated against 88 Integrated Values Survey countries, the answer is often no. NSR exceeds 1.0 on 49 of 117 valid model-question pairs

translated_title: 大语言模型文化对齐中的测量效度
translated_abstract: 研究人员越来越多地将大语言模型（LLM）的调查问卷回答作为人类文化价值观的替代指标。这包括将模型输出投影到英格尔哈特-韦尔策尔文化地图等工具上，并据此得出模型与哪些文化相似的结论。虽然模型对带有价值取向问题的回答可以被解读为一种文化信号，但它同时包含抽样噪声，并且对问题的表述方式可能相当敏感。在本文中，我们针对多个大语言模型，将调查回答、抽样噪声和问题表述三个因素分离开来。我们将这些模型的回答方差分解为跨随机种子和提示词改写的变异。我们采用噪声信号比（NSR）来检验模型表面上呈现的文化位置是否能够与噪声区分开来。当该方法应用于来自四个地理来源的十余个模型，并以88个综合价值观调查国家数据进行校准时，答案往往是否定的：在117个有效的模型-问题配对中，有49个的NSR超过了1.0。
tldr: 该论文提出噪声信号比（NSR）方法，将大语言模型调查回答中的抽样噪声和问题表述影响与文化信号分离，发现117个有效模型-问题配对中有49个的NSR超过1.0，表明模型表面上呈现的文化定位常常无法与噪声区分，从而质疑了用LLM调查回答代理人类文化价值观的测量效度。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a noise-to-signal ratio (NSR) method to disentangle cultural signals from sampling noise and question framing effects in LLM survey responses, finding that NSR exceeds 1.0 in 49 of 117 valid model-question pairs, revealing that models' apparent cultural positions are often indistinguishable from noise and challenging the measurement validity of using LLM survey responses as proxies for human cultural values.
